roadmapTask: Plan horizon 10 of the agent-agnostic-browser-bridge project. Add a CDP-based scroll page action (scrollPage) to the tools/chrome-bridge package that materializes virtualized / lazy-rendered list rows the ISOLATED-world DOM-read path (readPage / getPageText / findElement) misses, shipped as one atomic page action end to end and reusing horizon 9's per-command chrome.debugger attach helper, verified by a live-Chrome head-to-head on a real virtualized list. Keep per-command attach/detach; do not touch the dead active-tab surface.

dimensionScores.evidence: Interface DebuggerPorts.scroll is exactly scroll(tabId: number, intent: ScrollIntent): Promise<ScrollOutcome> with no other new members; ScrollIntent is exactly two optional readonly fields amountPx/toBottom (no direction/repeat), ScrollOutcome exactly four readonly fields with method literally 'wheel'|'script'|'none'; both exported and named in debugger-ports.unit.test.ts. ABOVE a 9: amountPx default is a named const SCROLL_DEFAULT_PIXELS=2000 applied via `intent.amountPx ?? SCROLL_DEFAULT_PIXELS` at the top of scrollTab BEFORE the toBottom branch, and deltaY is resolved after that (`toBottom ? scrollHeight : amountPx`) so the toBottom branch can never bypass it into a NaN deltaY; toBottom is a single window.scrollTo(0, document.documentElement.scrollHeight) jump, not a loop.

The wheel-only test pins the full Input.dispatchMouseEvent byte-for-byte ({type:'mouseWheel', x:640, y:400, deltaX:0, deltaY:2000}), pins Runtime.evaluate reads with returnByValue/awaitPromise, deltaY=2000 default and deltaY=5000 (scrollHeight) on toBottom, and asserts the exact fallback expressions window.scrollBy(0, 2000)/window.scrollTo(0, document.documentElement.scrollHeight). NOT a 10: x/y are asserted as hardcoded literals 640/400 matching the stub fixture (innerWidth 1280 / innerHeight 800) rather than asserted to be derived from the stubbed first read-back (no explicit x === Math.round(innerWidth/2)) — matches the rubric's literal-x/y failure example. Score 8.

scroll() calls withDebuggerSession(tabId, 'scrolling', () => scrollTab(...)) and all CDP work (wheel dispatch, both settle delays, both metrics read-backs, fallback, outcome) runs inside that run callback; the label union is widened to include 'scrolling'. ABOVE a 9: the success path asserts attach({tabId},'1.3')+detach, the error path asserts detach still runs on a rejected sendCommand and re-attach works after a failure (attachSpy toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)), the onDetach listener is asserted registered once only, and a mid-command detach rejection explicitly asserts the message 'while scrolling' (built from the live entry.label, not a shared 'evaluating' constant). No module/instance attach state added outside withDebuggerSession.

Three explicit branch tests exist: wheel-only (asserts the scrollBy fallback is NEVER sent and method==='wheel'), wheel-then-script-fallback (fallback IS sent, method==='script'), neither-moved (method==='none'); scrollYBefore/scrollYAfter are the actual first/final read-back values (0/2000, 0/2000, 0/0). ABOVE a 9: movedBy uses a tolerance comparison Math.abs(to-from) >= SCROLL_MOVE_TOLERANCE (0.5) rather than strict equality, and reachedEnd is computed with a small slack (scrollY + innerHeight >= scrollHeight - SCROLL_END_SLACK) with both true (toBottom test) and false (wheel test) covered.

Both fake implementers were updated: fakeDebugger in page-actions.unit.test.ts and fakeDebuggerPorts in service-worker.unit.test.ts each carry a scroll stub returning { method:'none' as const, scrollYBefore:0, scrollYAfter:0, reachedEnd:false }, structurally satisfying ScrollOutcome. git status shows service-worker.ts source itself unchanged (only its test file), and `npm run verify` exits 0 (tsc --noEmit clean, eslint --max-warnings 0 clean, 280 tests / 22 files). ABOVE a 9: the full verify is green with zero suppressions — no @ts-expect-error, no it.skip, no `as` casts — and the method literal is `as const`-typed so it narrows to ScrollOutcome['method'] under strict.

parseScrollMetrics narrows the reply through the shared module isRecord guard plus a finite() numeric guard (typeof number && Number.isFinite, else 0) — no `result.result.value as number`, no any, no !, no `as <type>` on the scroll path; isRecord is reused (module helper), not re-implemented inline; the settle-delay evaluate result (sleepTab) is not parsed for a value it does not need. ABOVE a 9: the degenerate-reply test resolves with method==='none' (not rejecting) and asserts Number.isFinite on both scrollYBefore and scrollYAfter, proving the numeric guards reject NaN instead of leaking it through.

phases.blockedReason: REPLAN_REQUIRED: verdict on the fixed scrollPage is now clear (retry attempt 2 continuation, 2026-09-03). The wedge is fixed (session timeout + guaranteed detach, and the bounded-wheel fix makes scrollPage scroll via Runtime.evaluate window.scrollBy when Input.dispatchMouseEvent hangs) — `npm run verify` green (290 tests). BUT the horizon's phase-3 verification premise is INVALIDATED: in the deliberately-unfocused sandbox tab the browser runs NO rendering pass, confirmed live on a trivial local page — window.scrollBy changes scrollY but fires zero scroll events, IntersectionObserver never fires, and content-visibility:auto never reveals (innerText stays empty after scrolling to row 500). No virtualized/lazy-rendered page responds to a scroll there, so scrollPage can move the window but CANNOT materialize rows a prior readPage missed. The verification is infeasible in the sandbox tab as designed. Horizon needs a revision: either create the sandbox tab so it actually renders (change tab creation/focus), or narrow the success criterion to 'scrollPage moves the window' and drop the materialization gate, or verify against a render-able tab.
